title: Affine data at a closed point of an integral locally finite-type scheme
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty integral scheme locally of finite type over $K$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points]. Let $\eta$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point], put $L=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], with its structural $K$-algebra structure, and put $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There is an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $A$ is a nonzero finitely generated $K$-algebra domain [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$ representing $x$, with the following properties. The point $\eta$ belongs to $U$ and the germ map $A\to L$ is a $K$-algebra map making $L$ a fraction field of $A$ (it is injective, every nonzero element of $A$ becomes invertible, and every element of $L$ is a quotient of two germs). Restriction gives a canonical isomorphism of local $K$-algebras $\mathcal O_{U,x}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$, hence a $K$-isomorphism $\kappa_U(x)\cong\kappa_X(x)$ of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. The extension $\kappa_X(x)/K$ is finite. Finally $r$ is a finite nonnegative integer and $\dim A=\dim A_{\mathfrak m}=r$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is the localization at $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood U of x using Mathlib exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset inside the top open. It is nonempty, so IsIntegral supplies IsDomain of its actual section ring. LocallyOfFiniteType.finiteType_appLE gives finite type for the structural map on U; compose with the inverse of ΓSpecIso, which is finite type because it is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type, in Section 01T0; affine cover of Spec K

proof.text: Apply Mathlib IsAffineOpen.primeIdealOf_isMaximal_of_isClosed to x in U and its given closedness in X. This gives maximality of the actual primeIdealOf used in the conclusion.

source.place: Tags 00DZ, definition-spectrum-ring, and 00E1, definition-Zariski-topology; closed sets V(I)

proof.text: Apply the Mathlib fraction-field leaf functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen to the nonempty affine open U. The genericPoint_spec criterion puts the generic point in U. germ_injective_of_isIntegral gives injectivity; nonzero germs are units in the function field. IsFractionRing.div_surjective supplies the quotient expression. The equation on structural constants is germ_res_apply for the inclusion U into the top open.

Choose exactly U.stalkIso at x as the stalk comparison and the inverse of asIso of the open immersion residueFieldMap as the residue-field comparison. Mathlib stalkIso_inv identifies the inverse stalk comparison with the inclusion stalkMap. Apply injectivity of that inverse and germ_stalkMap_apply to prove compatibility with structural constants. For residue constants use the already proved Scheme.Hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap_comp from WeilConjectures.PointCount and cancel residueFieldMap with its inverse. Thus the chosen comparisons are precisely the canonical maps required, with the two K-compatibility equations.

Reuse the already proved source theorem Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_isClosed from WeilConjectures.PointCount, applied to f and the given closed point x. This is the Jacobson/Zariski lemma argument and supplies Module.Finite for exactly f.residueFieldAlgebraMap, without reconstructing or choosing a quotient comparison.

source.place: Tag 00FV, theorem-nullstellensatz (1); maximal quotient of a finite-type algebra

proof.text: Give Γ(X,U) its structural K-algebra and install its finite-type instance from step 1. Give X.functionField the precise structural algebra in the conclusion. The germ equation on constants from step 3 establishes IsScalarTower K Γ(X,U) X.functionField. Apply finiteType_domain_ringKrullDim_eq_trdeg to Γ(X,U); it gives a natural number r with ring dimension r, FractionRing transcendence degree r and dimension r for every maximal localization. Restrict the canonical FractionRing.algEquiv to K using this scalar tower; AlgEquiv.trdeg_eq transports the transcendence degree to X.functionField. Apply the maximal-localization clause to the maximal prime from step 2.
